notes: This is a compact snapshot of the parser output for the user-reported fee mismatch cases.
Numeric paper_fee and online_fee keep the first dollar amount for DB compatibility.
Use paper_fee_text, online_fee_text, and fee_details when Excel needs exact USCIS text such as '$1,500 or $750'.

issue_1_missing_category.behavior: When USCIS has no Filing Category/Category column, filing_category is blank instead of invented as General Filing.

last_rows.filing_category: Additional Fees: If you are filing as a Nonprofit;
Additional Fees: If you are filing as a Small Employer.

issue_3_i129_h2a.form: I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker - H-2A Petitions (Including Standalone I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker: H-2A Classification)

first_two_rows.filing_category: If you are filing an H-2A petition with named workers. (limited to 25 beneficiaries per petition)
If you are filing an H-2A petition with named workers. (limited to 25 beneficiaries per petition) — If you are filing as a Small Employer or Nonprofit.

issue_4_i129_h1b_h1b1.form: I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker – H-1B and H-1B1 Petitions

corrected_rows.filing_category: Additional Fees: H-1B petitioners must submit a Fraud Prevention and Detection fee if they are: Seeking initial approval of H-1B nonimmigrant status for a beneficiary; or Seeking approval to employ an H-1B nonimmigrant currently working for another petitioner. Petitioners for Chile or Singapore H-1B1 Free Trade Nonimmigrants do not have to pay the Fraud Prevention and Detection fee. Fraud Prevention and Detection fee, when applicable, may not be waived.

Additional Fees: American Competitiveness and Workforce Improvement Act (ACWIA). Petitioners filing for: An H-1B nonimmigrant; or A Chile or Singapore H-1B1 Free Trade Nonimmigrant must submit an additional ACWIA fee unless they are exempt under Section 2 of the H-1B Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement. To determine which ACWIA fee to pay, complete Section 2 of the H-1B Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement.
corrected_rows.paper_fee_text: $1,500 or $750 (depending on number of workers the petitioner employs)
corrected_rows.online_fee_text: $1,500 or $750 (depending on number of workers the petitioner employs)

corrected_rows.filing_category: Additional Fees: Presidential Proclamation on Restriction of Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers. Do not submit payment for this fee with your petition. You must use pay.gov to pay this fee prior to filing your petition. For additional information, see our H-1B Specialty Occupations page.
corrected_rows.online_fee_text: $100,000 (unless an exception has been granted by the Secretary of Homeland Security)

issue_5_i129_l_l1.form: I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker – L and L-1 Petitions

second_form_row.filing_category: If you are filing L petitions. — If you are filing as a Small Employer or Nonprofit.

additional_condition_rows_are_not_split.filing_category: Additional Fees: L petitioners must submit a Fraud Prevention and Detection fee if they are: Seeking initial approval of L nonimmigrant status for a beneficiary; Seeking approval to employ an L nonimmigrant currently working for another petitioner; or For blanket petitions, seeking approval for an L nonimmigrant to continue employment with an entity different from the previous petitioner.

Additional Fees: L-1 petitioners are required to submit an additional fee mandated by Public Law 114-113, if: They are required to submit the Fraud Prevention and Detection fee; They employ 50 or more individuals in the United States; and More than 50 percent of those employees are in H-1B, L-1A, or L-1B nonimmigrant status.

issue_6_i131_advance_parole.form: I-131, Application for Travel Documents, Parole Documents, and Arrival/Departure Records – Advance Parole Document

last_row.filing_category: Additional Fee if Approved: Pub. L. 119-21 Immigration Parole Fee Each time you seek parole at a port of entry (POE), U.S. Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) will require you to pay an additional fee at the POE, unless they determine that you qualify for an exception.
